JUDGMENT:
1. The order impugned in this appeal is dated 30.12.2022 of Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (referred as AO) holding appellants responsible for violation on various terms and conditions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and imposing penalties on them.
BRIEF FACTS 2.
The brief facts of the case are that on 15.10.2018, the FSO bought a sample of "Foxnuts" from the appellants.

The sample consisted 12 containers of 100 gm each, same were divided into four counterparts by pouring equally into four clean and dry glass bottles, fastened and sealed according to rules and regulations, signed by the FBO and sample was taken as required and designated officer code slip was pasted on all.
One of the sample was sent to Food Analyst on 16.10.2018 and the rest counterparts were deposited in sealed packet with the designated officer.

The Food Analyst submitted the report on 29.10.2018 and found the sample to be "Misbranded" as there was violation of provision of 23 (1), Section 26 (1), Section 26 (2) (ii) read with Section 3 (1) (zf) and violated Section 27(3) (c) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

M/s. Sun Organic Industries Pvt. Ltd.
has also violated Section 27(1) of the FSS Act, 2003, which is punishable under Section 52 of the Act,
2006.
3. An opportunity was given to appellant to file an appeal under Section 46 (4) of the Act against the aforesaid report by the Designated Officer but no concerned person turned up for the same.

4. AO has held that appellant no. 8 has violated Section 27 (1) of the FSS Act, 2003 which is punishable under Section 52 FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation No. 2.3.24 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation's, 2011 and other appellants have violated Section 23(1), Section 26(1), Section 26(2) (ii) read with Section 3 (1) (zf) of the FSS Act, 2006.

sentences.text: Accordingly, appellant no. 1 to 5 and 7 were levied penalty of Rs. 25,000/- each and appellant nos. 6 and 8 were levied penalty of Rs. 50,000/- each.

GROUNDS OF CHALLANGE:
5. The Adjudicating Officer has passed the impugned order without application of mind.
The allegation "the best before shall be written in Capital Letter" was not mentioned as minor labeling defects and cannot be put in misbranded category.

It is stated that opinion of public analyst is based on complete misinterpretation of the provision of law and report of the Food Analyst lacks evidentary value and beyond Kailash Chand Pandey And Others vs Food Safety Officer Naresh Kumar Sharma on 28 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183849052/

sentences.text: the scope of the FSS Act, 2006.
It is urged that proper procedure prescribed by law has neither been adopted by the FSO/Department nor by the Adjudicating Officer.

6. Heard the arguments of Ld. Counsel of appellants and Chief Public Prosecutor and perused the material place on record by the appellant and the record of the Adjudicating Officer.
7.
The case of the respondent is based on Food Analyst report dated 29.10.2018.
The allegations made in this report i.e. of the label best before not declared in Capital Letters are accepted by the appellants.
The sole plea raised by the appellant is that this does not fall in the category of misbranding.

In support of his submissions, Ld.
Counsel for appellants has relied upon two letters dated 17.07.2018 and 17.01.2020 by the Director (Regulatory Compliance) and Deputy Director (RCD) to all Commissioner of Food Safety of all States/UTs.
8. For better appreciation of facts, the contents of both these letters are reproduced as follows:-

fssai File No. 1 (56) 2015/Advisory/FSSAI [Pt-1] Food Safety and Standards Authority of India A Statutory Authority established under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 FDA Bhawan, Kotla Road, New Delhi-11002 Dated 17.07.2018 To, The Commissioners of Food Safety, All States/Uts

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Subject: Rectification process for cases of minor labeling defects-reg.

Sir/Madam, It has come to the notice of FSSAI that the food safety authorities in some States have initiated adjudication proceedings against Food Business Operators (FBOs) for labeling defects of insignificant nature which could easily be rectified by following the process delineated under Scheme 32 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Resorting to adjudication proceedings in such cases not only causes avoidable harassment of FBOs but also is a waste of scarce resources of enforsement machinery of States/UTs, which could be utilized more meaningfully elsewhere to ensure safe and nutritious food to the citizen.
State/UT governments are, therefore, advised to take action under Section 32 of FSS Act in cases involving minor labelling defects which do not endanger food safety.
Yours Faithfully, (Garima Singh) Director (Regulatory Compliance) Tel. 23220990 Fssai No. 15 (28) 2020

/ Advisory/RCD/FSSAI Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (A Statutory body under Ministry of Health and Family Welfare)(Regulatory Compliance Division) FDA Bhavan, Kotla Road, New Dellhi-110002

sentences.text:
Under Chapter 2 Regulations 5 (10)
(a) runs as follows:-
(a) " Date of manufacture or packaging" and "Expiry/Use by" shall be declared on the label.
However, expression "Best before" may also be used as optional or additional information.
11. Admittedly by prosecution the requirement of mentioning the best before the date in Capital Letters has been discontinued in new regulations of 2020.
Coming back to the facts of the present case, as per the record, the date of inspection by Food Safety Officer is 15.10.2018.

As already discussed in its letter dated 17.07.2018 titled "Regulatory Compliance of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India", FSSAI has specifically mentioned that in the labeling defects of insignificant nature which could easily be rectified, the process under Section 32 of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 should be resorted to.

entities.text: Regulatory Compliance of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the subsequent letter dated 17.01.2020 FASSI at serial no. 6 has mentioned that non compliance in respect of Capital letters is a minor labeling defects for which compliance measures shall be initiated through improvement notice.
12. Under the scheme of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, in Chapter no. 7 Section 32 provides Improvement Notices.
For better appreciation of facts, the contents of Section are reproduced as follows.

(2) If the food business operator fails to comply with an improvement notice,
his licence may be suspended.

(3) If the food business operator still fails to comply with the improvement notice, the Designated Officer may, after giving the licensee an opportunity to show cause, cancel the licence granted to him:

sentences.text: Provided that the Designated Officer may suspend any licence forthwith in the interest of public health for reasons to be recorded in writing.

(4) Any person who is aggrieved by -
(a) an improvement notice; or (b) refusal to issue a certificate as to improvement; or (c) cancellation or suspension or revocation of licence under this Act, may appeal to the Commissioner of Food Safety whose decision thereon, shall be final.

(5) The period within which such an appeal may be brought shall be- (a) fifteen days from the date on which notice of the decision was served on the person desiring to appeal; or (b) in the case of an appeal under sub-section (1), the said period or the period specified in the improvement notice, whichever expires earlier.

Explanation-For the purpose of this sub-section, the making of the complaint shall be deemed to be the bringing of the appeal.
13.
As per this Section, Designated Officer was required to give an Improvement Notice, after noticing labeling defects, to the food business operator.
As already discussed in the above paras, the labeling defect found in this case can be put in the category of insignificant nature.

As the inspection happened on 15.10.2018 which was subsequent to the letter dated 17.07.2018 of Director (Regulatory Compliance), the Designated Officer was required to give an Improvement Notice and admittedly same was not given in this case.

14. As admitted by Ld. Counsel for appellant the new Food Safety and Standards (Labeling Display 2020) Act, has come into the effect and mentioning of best before in Capital Letter on the label has been dispensed with.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Labeling Display 2020) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The law mostly has prospective effect.
Here as discussed above, the Food Safety Officer/Designated Officer was required to give improvement notice under Section 32 of the Act which he failed to give.
But instead of that, directly a complaint was made to Adjudicating Officer.

Adjudicating Officer has also failed to appreciate the subsequent letter of the FSSAI dated 17.07.2018 and 17.01.2020 categorizing the non compliance in respect of Capital Letters as a defect of insignificant nature.

DECISION:
15.
In view of the facts and circumstances, the impugned order is set aside.
The amount deposited by the appellant be refunded.
